name: OPA197IDBVR
title: OPA197, OPA2197, OPA4197: 36 V precision op amps with rail-to-rail inputs and outputs
summary: Single, dual and quad op amps for 4.5 V to 36 V supplies whose inputs and outputs reach both rails. Offset is trimmed to 100 µV maximum (25 µV typical) with 2.5 µV/°C maximum drift; bias current is 5 pA typical, bandwidth 10 MHz, slew rate 20 V/µs and supply current 1 mA per amplifier. The inputs stand 36 V between them, the output drives 65 mA and 1 nF directly, and thermal shutdown guards the die. OPA197IDBVR is the single OPA197 in the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) on a 3000-piece reel, marked 12MV.

circuits.title: Follower with an isolation resistor for capacitive loads
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower on split supplies whose feedback is taken straight from the amplifier output, with RISO in series between that output and a purely capacitive load. RISO changes the open-loop response and raises phase margin; for loads from 100 pF to 1 µF, RISO values for 45° and 60° margin are listed with the measured overshoot. A resistive load in parallel with CLOAD forms a divider with RISO, so the output carries a gain error in proportion to RISO / RL.

parts.note: chosen with CLOAD: 47 Ω (45°) or 360 Ω (60°) at 100 pF down to 2.0 Ω or 4.7 Ω at 1 µF

circuits.title: Slew-rate limiter with one extra amplifier
circuits.description: Two OPA197s on VCC and VEE limit the slew rate of VOUT symmetrically, the same rising and falling, so the load voltage ramps up and down instead of stepping. U1 is the gain stage, with VIN on its inverting input and VOUT fed back to its non-inverting input. U2 takes U1's output through R2 into its inverting input, with C1 in series with R1 as its feedback. RL is the 10 kΩ load.

circuits.title: Precision 2.5 V reference buffer driving 10 µF
circuits.description: The amplifier buffers a 2.5 V reference into a 10 µF ceramic load on a single VCC supply. RISO, 37.4 Ω, separates the amplifier output from CL. DC feedback comes from VOUT through RF; high-frequency feedback comes from the amplifier output through RFx and CF. With these values the closed-loop bandwidth at VOUT is 4 kHz and loop-gain phase margin is 89°; another load capacitance calls for new RF, RFx, CF and RISO.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypassing
circuits.description: The OPA197 in the 8-pin package as a non-inverting stage: VIN drives +IN, RG runs from -IN to ground and RF from -IN to the output. Each supply pin has a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor to ground; on a single supply only the V+ capacitor is needed. RF and RG sit next to -IN to keep its parasitic capacitance low.

circuits.title: Buffer heating itself into thermal protection
circuits.description: A unity-gain buffer on a single +30 V supply holds 3 V across a 100 Ω load, so it sources 30 mA and dissipates 0.81 W. At 65°C ambient and 116°C/W this predicts a 159°C junction; instead the output turns off near 140°C, falls to 0 V through RL, and cycles back on as the die cools.
notes: TA = 65°C, PD = 0.81 W, θJA = 116°C/W, IOUT = 30 mA.

operation.text: OPA197 is one amplifier, OPA2197 two and OPA4197 four, all specified from -40°C to +125°C and run from 4.5 V to 36 V (±2.25 V to ±18 V). Inputs and output reach both rails, offset is ±25 µV typical, bandwidth 10 MHz, slew rate 20 V/µs, quiescent current 1 mA per amplifier.
OPA197-Q1, OPA2197-Q1 and OPA4197-Q1 are automotive versions qualified to AEC-Q100.

Inputs pass through a 36-V differential front end into parallel N-channel and P-channel input stages, then a slew-boost stage, compensation for heavy capacitive loads and the output stage. Offset is trimmed at two temperatures.

No back-to-back clamp diodes sit across the inputs, so the full 36 V supply span may appear between +IN and -IN. A conventional amplifier's clamps conduct on fast input steps (for example after a multiplexer switches), drawing current through the source filter and stretching settling; this input does not, so it settles quickly after channel changes and can serve as a comparator.
The inputs carry built-in EMI filtering. EMIRR at +IN, measured from 10 MHz to 6 GHz with -10 dBm applied, ±18 V supplies and VCM = 0 V, rises from 44.1 dB at 400 MHz to 105.5 dB at 5 GHz.
Driving an input past either rail does not reverse the output; the output stays limited at the matching rail.

Junction temperature must not exceed 150°C. A sensor turns the output drive off above about 140°C; the output goes high-impedance until the die cools, then resumes, cycling as long as the overload lasts.

At unity gain the output drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitance directly; higher gain tolerates more. For more margin at unity gain, a 10 Ω to 20 Ω resistor in series with the output cuts ringing while keeping dc accuracy; with a resistive load as well, the error grows with RISO / RL. Uses include reference buffers, MOSFET gate drive and cable-shield drive.

The input range runs 100 mV past each rail. The P-channel pair works from 100 mV below V- up to about (V+) - 1.5 V, the N-channel pair from about (V+) - 3 V to 100 mV above V+. Between (V+) - 3 V and (V+) - 1.5 V both pairs conduct; there offset, drift, CMRR, PSRR, noise and THD can be worse, and the region shifts somewhat from part to part. Each pair has its own precision trim, so the step in offset across the transition stands out against the low offset elsewhere.

Each input reaches the amplifier through 100 Ω inside the part. Steering diodes run from the inputs and output to the internal supply lines, which meet at an absorption cell that clamps the supplies during ESD. These parts guard against short, high-voltage ESD (about 1 kV for 100 ns) out of circuit, not against long overstress (about 50 V for 100 ms) in circuit. In a board, current-limiting resistors on the inputs and TVS diodes on the supplies keep the absorption cell from firing.
When the output saturates it takes about 200 ns to come back to linear operation, after which it slews at the normal rate.
With 100 mV overdrive, propagation delay is 0.97 µs on a rising output edge and 1.1 µs on a falling one.
There is one mode: the amplifier runs whenever the supply exceeds 4.5 V (±2.25 V), up to 36 V (±18 V).

OPA197 buffers each of four ±20 V differential inputs ahead of a 4:2 multiplexer and drives the attenuating level shifter into a 16-bit 400 kSPS SAR ADC (ADS8864), with OPA140 and OPA350 in the ADC driver and common-mode paths and a REF3240 reference. The design runs on ±15 V, the ADC on 3.3 V with a 4.096 V reference, and each input carries 10 V peak at 10 kHz. The aims: low-impedance input filters, fast settling after channel switching, a stable attenuating driver and a low-drift reference driver.
Specified from 4.5 V to 36 V (±2.25 V to ±18 V); above 40 V the part can be damaged. Place a 0.1 µF capacitor at each supply pin.

Low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramics from each supply pin to ground, close to the part; one from V+ is enough on a single supply. Use a ground plane and keep digital and analog return currents apart. Route input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing at right angles where they must cross. Place RF and RG against the inverting input. A driven guard ring around high-impedance nodes reduces leakage. Clean the board after assembly; after aqueous cleaning, bake at 85°C for 30 minutes to drive out moisture.
